title: Red, cracked hands in a woman of seventy-two; her carer, a pharmacy technician and a voice from the corridor; creams she cannot name
description: Fictional synthetic consultation for Module 3 testing; not a real patient record or medical advice.

design.opening: the doctor greets the carer first, thinking he is the patient's son
design.patient_style: hesitant, forgetful, defers to her carer
partial_or_uncertain: how long the hands have been bad: she says since the spring, the carer says since Christmas, the pharmacy technician remembers a visit in August
she cannot name the cream that helped; she describes it as the white one in the tube with a blue lid
she stopped one cream herself and is not sure when
an unidentified woman's voice interrupts from the corridor and is never identified
which of her two tablets is for cholesterol and which for fluid is muddled
facts: red, cracked hands, blisters between fingers, drier skin that has settled
denies a new soap or cream, oozing, fever, joint pain, rash elsewhere, nail changes
tonsils out as a teenager, son has asthma, brother has epilepsy
smokes about eight a day, fast food at lunch
red, dry, cracked skin in the finger creases, no weeping
plan: patch test on a Wednesday at 10, review in three weeks
